text:
sam: Heads up  found another streaming leak in the Python SDK when callers rely on GC to close async generators. Repro on 3.11/3.12 where async generator finalizers don't run in time and sockets stay open.
maria: Oof. Is this the same as the earlier weakref/finalize issue or a different codepath?
sam: Related but different surface. This is our AsyncIteratorAdapter that wraps a sync iterator into an async generator using an executor. We attach a weakref.finalize to the adapter to close the underlying sync iterator on GC. Minimal repro below:
```python
import asyncio, weakref, socket

class SyncStream:
    def __init__(self):
        self.s = socket.socket()
        self.s.connect(('127.0.0.1', 9001))
    def __iter__(self):
        return self
    def __next__(self):
        data = self.s.recv(1024)
        if not data:
            raise StopIteration
        return data
    def close(self):
        self.s.close()

async def adapter(sync_it):
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    def it_next():
        return next(sync_it)
    while True:
        try:
            chunk = await loop.run_in_executor(None, it_next)
        except StopIteration:
            break
        yield chunk

async def main():
    s = SyncStream()
    ref = weakref.finalize(s, s.close)
    ag = adapter(iter(s))
    # consume one chunk then drop reference
    await anext(ag)
    del s
    # force GC and short sleep
    import gc, time
    gc.collect()
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    # check fds outside (run lsof in shell)

asyncio.run(main())
```
sam: On CI we sometimes see the FD still open (verified with lsof) even after gc.collect() + loop run. Looks flaky across platforms.
josh: Could be executor thread holding frame that references socket until thread finishes. Also finalizer scheduling may not be immediate.
maria: Two fixes: 1) make adapter return an async context manager so callers do `async with client.stream(...) as s:` and we call close deterministically; 2) ensure adapter itself calls close in its aclose() / __anext__ stop path so executor threads don't hold reference.
sam: Agreed. Proposed change in SDK samples and docs to prefer `async with`. Also add a runtime warning when a stream is garbage-collected without being closed (include allocation stack).
josh: For the SDK internals, add an explicit `.aclose()` that cancels outstanding executor futures and closes the sync iterator. Also add a small stress test that creates+drops 1000 streams and asserts FD delta is zero.
maria: We should also add a lint check in sample apps (devex rule) and update quickstarts. People will copy-paste naive `ag = client.stream(...); await anext(ag)` patterns.
sam: I'll open internal issue internal#2024 and draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1002 (WIP). I'll add tests that run the fake TCP server in-process and assert no lingering connections after stream close.
josh: One more thought  capture allocation stack when creating adapter so warning can point to callsite. We'll gate that behind DEBUG=1 to avoid perf hit.
sam: Added to checklist: (1) make stream an async context manager, (2) implement aclose to cancel executor futures, (3) add GC-finalizer fallback that logs stack, (4) add CI stress test, (5) update samples/quickstart.
sam: Pasting quick lsof output from repro run: 
"COMMAND   PID   USER   FD   TYPE DEVICE SIZE/OFF NODE NAME
python   8521   ubuntu  12u  IPv4  56789      0t0  TCP 127.0.0.1:52345->127.0.0.1:9001 (ESTABLISHED)"
maria: Thanks. Can you also try reproducing without executor (pure async server) to rule out thread timing?
sam: Yep. Repro still intermittent but less frequent; executor seems to worsen it. Will include both variants in tests.
